name: net_rejoin_keeps_level
description: A rejoin builds the same level (M8, contract-m8 §3 and §5): a High Water dev match at Hard, two seats played by the plan bots; MATCH_CONFIG's difficulty 1 makes each client's level Hard and its simulation's rules Hard's. Client 2's game is killed past a kept checkpoint and started again from user://net.cfg alone (no level kept there): MATCH_CONFIG(rejoin) names the match's own level, so the game started again builds Hard's rules, loads the checkpoint the RESYNC(rejoin) brings and its hashes agree from it on. A client whose MATCH_CONFIG(rejoin) names another level than the match it kept fails rather than plays on, and so does one whose link was lost while the match loaded and whose plain MATCH_CONFIG names another level (at the match's own it keeps its world), and so does one told to play a duel at Hard (a mode without levels plays Normal).

steps.msg: MATCH_CONFIG names the match's level, Hard
each client plays Hard and builds Hard's rules: its numbers, not only its name (the rules track's table)
a checkpoint past tick 0 is kept
the killed game's seat went AWAY
started again, the game knows only its seat: no level yet
MATCH_CONFIG(rejoin) and RESYNC(rejoin) from a checkpoint past tick 0

steps.assert: int(scene.client(2).config['difficulty']) == 1 and scene.client(2).difficulty == 'hard' and scene.client(2).sim.rules['difficulty'] == 'hard' and MR.level_problem(scene.client(2).sim.rules) == '' and scene.client(2).sim.rules['lives'] == scene.client(1).sim.rules['lives']
steps.msg: the rejoin's MATCH_CONFIG names Hard, and the game started again builds Hard's rules, numbers and all
every hash from the checkpoint on agrees: the same rules on both

steps.assert: c.phase_name() == 'LOADING' and c.difficulty == 'hard' and c.sim.rules['difficulty'] == 'hard' and MR.level_problem(c.sim.rules) == ''
steps.msg: a client builds the match from its config at Hard
a rejoin's MATCH_CONFIG at another level than the world it kept fails the link

steps.assert: e.phase_name() == 'LOADING' and not e.reconnecting and e.difficulty == 'hard' and e.sim.rules['difficulty'] == 'hard'
steps.msg: the link lost while the match loads, a plain MATCH_CONFIG at the match's own level keeps the world standing
and one at another level fails the link, as a rejoin's does: the world standing is the other level's
a duel at Hard is no match this game plays: a mode without levels plays Normal
